desc:
Among all strings that are subsequences of both s and t and that also contain pattern as a subsequence, find the length of the longest one.

Return -1 if no common subsequence of s and t contains pattern. An empty pattern is contained in every string, so then the answer is the ordinary longest common subsequence length.

s = "abcbdab", t = "bdcaba", pattern = "ba"  ->  4   ("bdab" contains b ... a)
s = "abcbdab", t = "bdcaba", pattern = "aa"  ->  3
s = "abcbdab", t = "bdcaba", pattern = "ac"  ->  -1  (no common subsequence has an a before a c)
constraints: All strings contain only lowercase English letters
hints: Without the pattern this is the ordinary longest common subsequence table. Which extra piece of information must a state remember to know whether the pattern is contained?

Add a third index k: let f[i][j][k] be the length of the longest common subsequence of the first i characters of s and the first j characters of t that contains the first k characters of the pattern as a subsequence (or minus infinity if none does).

When s[i-1] == t[j-1] == c, you can append c either as a plain extra character, from f[i-1][j-1][k], or, if c == pattern[k-1], as the last character needed for the first k pattern characters, from f[i-1][j-1][k-1]. The answer is f[m][n][len(pattern)].
editorial: Extend the LCS table with the number k of pattern characters that must be contained. Define f[i][j][k] as the maximum length of a common subsequence of s[:i] and t[:j] that contains pattern[:k] as a subsequence, and minus infinity if there is none. The base cases are f[i][j][0] = the plain LCS (starting from 0 for the empty prefix) and f[i][j][k] = -inf for k > 0 when one prefix is empty.

For the transition, an optimal string either does not use s[i-1] (value f[i-1][j][k]), does not use t[j-1] (value f[i][j-1][k]), or ends with a character matched to both of them, which requires s[i-1] == t[j-1] = c. Remove that last character c from the string. What is left is a common subsequence of the shorter prefixes. If it still contains pattern[:k], the value is f[i-1][j-1][k] + 1. Otherwise the string contained pattern[:k] only thanks to the final c, which forces c == pattern[k-1] and the rest to contain pattern[:k-1], so the value is f[i-1][j-1][k-1] + 1.

The final answer is f[m][n][L] with L the pattern length, or -1 when that is minus infinity. The table has m · n · (L + 1) cells with O(1) work each. Keeping only the previous row of i reduces memory to O(n · L).
